whatItIs.text: The lean white meat of the chicken, the most common poultry in the world and the second most eaten meat after pork.

historyNote.text: Chickens descend from red junglefowl raised thousands of years ago in the northern Indian subcontinent; in the 1800s chicken was so costly in America that it was a rich person's dish, and only after a Second World War beef and pork shortage did everyday consumption take off.

howToChoose.text: Look for plump, pink fillets with firm flesh and no grey or sticky patches; skinless boneless is the most convenient, skin-on bone-in the most forgiving to cook.

storage.text: Raw chicken is a keep-it-cold-and-separate ingredient: store on the bottom shelf and cook within the rulebook's window.
storage.note: raw-poultry storage and handling live in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Cooked breast shredded into soup, tacos, or fried rice stretches one fillet into two meals; poach instead of roast if it is already dry.

substitutions.note: fattier and harder to overcook; ~2-3 minutes longer to cook
